title: introduce-intake-annotations-variant-compatibility-hints-and-performance-fingerprint
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: onboarding teams need machine-readable hints about which model variants are mutually compatible (quantization/kv-cache shape/sequence-length bounds) and an automated per-intake performance fingerprint so release notes can surface expected latency/cost deltas. This PR adds a compatibility-hints field to the model manifest, a perf_fingerprint snapshot recorded at intake time, and a small automation that synthesizes changelog blurb candidates based on delta between fingerprints. Changes include schema, ingestion hook, release-note generator, tests, and migration. Checklist: - [x] define compatibility-hints schema and docs - [x] ingest hints at model intake and persist in manifest store - [x] capture perf_fingerprint from profiler snapshot hook - [x] generate candidate release-note lines and severity tags - [x] add unit/integration tests and sample manifests - [x] migration element for existing manifests - [x] update onboarding docs and examples Rollout plan: roll out ingestion as a non-blocking annotation and surface hints in the registry UI; after 2 weeks flip a flag to enforce hint presence for new manifests. Rollback: remove flag and drop automated release-note drafts; compatible with prior manifest schema. Why unique: existing onboarding focuses on static metadata; this ties performance deltas to onboarding and makes changelogs actionable for SRE and Release Engineering. Links: linear/ENG-3241, support ticket SUP-447. No user-visible API changes to runtime; only registry intake and admin console surfaces are affected.
commits: feat(onboard): add compatibility_hints schema and validation
feat(onboard): record perf_fingerprint from profiler on intake
feat(release-notes): generate delta-based candidate blurbs with severity tags
test(onboard): add manifest parser and compatibility mapping tests
docs(onboard): onboarding guide for compatibility hints and examples
migrations: add column compat_hint and perf_fingerprint to manifests table
review_comments: Jonah Kim: This looks promising. Can you expand tests to cover transitive variant compatibility (A compatible with B and B with C implies A with C)?
Author (Aisha): Good catch, added transitive mapping unit test and a comment explaining the conservative merge semantics.
Marcus Li: Concern: adding perf_fingerprint to every intake increases manifest size and DB churn. Can we store only compressed deltas?
Author (Aisha): Addressed by compressing the fingerprint and keeping an LZ4 column; migration script includes a compact serializer. Left full snapshot optional behind a feature flag for debugging.
Sofia Ortega: Docs are clear. Please add a short paragraph about how Release Engineers should interpret severity tags.
Author (Aisha): Added guidance and examples in docs/onboard/compatibility-guidelines.md. Ready for approval.
ci_details: integration: initial run failed on infra flaky DB migration (timeout). Reran and passed
e2e-onboard-harness: pass (sample manifests ingested, UI surfaces hints)
summary_changes: Add compatibility_hints field to model manifest schema with conservative typing and optional entries
Capture perf_fingerprint at intake using existing profiler hook and compress for storage
Introduce generate_diff_blurb automation that compares new fingerprint to baseline and suggests release-note lines with severity tags (minor/medium/major)
Migration script to add new columns and compact existing snapshots behind feature flag
Update onboarding docs and examples with recommended guidance and rollouts
Add unit/integration tests including transitive compatibility mapping
qa_notes: Manual QA: ingested 6 sample manifests (open-source and quantized variants), verified UI shows compatibility hints and release-note drafts; SRE ran a 1k-request perf sweep to ensure profiler hook is non-blocking. Automated tests added for reading/writing compressed fingerprints and delta calculation. Monitoring: added temporary alert on manifest write latency before and after rollout.
risk_and_rollback: Risk: increased DB storage and potential write latency during high-throughput onboard spikes. Mitigations: compressed storage, non-blocking hook, feature-flagged full-snapshot. Rollback: drop UI feature flag and remove auto-draft generation; run migration reversal to remove added columns if required. Estimated rollback time: < 2 hours for UI flag flip, < 6 hours for DB migration revert depending on replication lag.
audience: model-registry team, release engineering, SRE, onboarding/solutions engineers
release_notes: Added manifest annotations: compatibility_hints and perf_fingerprint. Registry will now surface suggested release-note blurbs describing expected perf/latency deltas on new model intake. Admins can opt-in to full snapshot recording via feature flag. (ENG-3241, SUP-447)
notes_for_release_engineers: When reviewing new model rollouts, check the generated severity tag and sample blurb. If a 'major' perf delta is suggested, run the profiler sweep in staging and consider canary routing. The generator is a helper not an enforcement mechanism.
post_merge_tasks: - Flip non-blocking flag to enforced after 2-week observation window - Add metric dashboard for perf_fingerprint delta distribution - Notify partners via #registry-release channel
backwards_compatibility: Manifests without compatibility_hints remain valid. Ingest treats hints as advisory for now. Migration adds nullable columns and is reversible.
notes: This PR aims to close the loop between onboarding metadata and release notes so downstream teams get actionable perf context at intake time. The approach favors conservative defaults and incremental rollout to minimize risk.
